text: So far, measuring a qubit has meant one specific thing: checking whether it's 0 or 1. That's just one choice out of infinitely many, and which basis you pick is itself a real, physically consequential decision.

The computational basis is the one every earlier lesson has used, but nothing forces you to measure that way. Any pair of states that's orthonormal — each normalized, and mutually orthogonal — can serve as a legitimate measurement basis. The Born rule still applies exactly the same way: the probability of a given outcome is the squared magnitude of the inner product between the qubit's state and that basis state.

Take ket-zero — about as definite as a state gets, with P of 0 equal to 1 in the computational basis. Now measure that same state in the X-basis, made of ket-plus and ket-minus. The overlap with ket-plus squared gives 0.5, and the overlap with ket-minus squared also gives 0.5 — a perfect coin flip. The identical pattern holds for ket-one. The qubit's actual state never changed; what changed is which question you asked of it.

It would be easy to dismiss this as bookkeeping, but that dismissal is wrong. The 50/50 split you get measuring ket-zero in the X-basis is a real, experimentally verifiable outcome — run it, and you really do get plus half the time and minus half the time, genuine randomness, not a relabeling of something secretly deterministic. Basis choice doesn't just redescribe the same facts; it changes which facts are definite and which are random.

Choosing a measurement basis is a real design decision in quantum algorithms. A circuit might deliberately rotate a qubit before measuring it in the computational basis — mathematically equivalent to measuring the original state in a rotated basis — specifically to extract the information that basis is sensitive to. You'll see this return in chapter 4, where entanglement and Bell-inequality tests are built entirely out of comparing statistics across different chosen bases.
Next lesson is a lab running the Born rule, collapse, and basis choice together on concrete worked problems.
